source.title: A suite of Vision Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: The text is readable and appears complete. It refers to plots, but the plots themselves are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports a qualitative comparison of sparse-autoencoder features across ViT layers, but does not test neuron poles, the share of interpretable neurons, or any other version of the claim.
record.gate_note: The reported layer-20 monosemanticity result concerns SAE features rather than the model's own neurons and gives no share of interpretable units. The reconstruction-MSE discussion concerns image-token positions, not the claim's subject.
record.test_reason: The post releases top-k SAEs trained on a CLIP ViT-L residual stream. It reports a qualitative layer ranking of SAE-feature monosemanticity. It does not examine the model's own neurons, report a share of interpretable neurons, compare architectures or tools for native neurons, build attribution graphs, or score neuron explanations. No version is tested. The relation is closer to cites_only/discusses than to tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say preliminary analysis suggests layer 20 is the most monosemantic layer, and that its features activate most frequently. They present it as a reasonable alternative to the commonly used layer 22. They also report that outer image tokens are easier to reconstruct than central ones, and they caution that nothing was shown rigorously.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains top-k sparse autoencoders on a vision transformer's residual stream and evaluates SAE features; it does not audit native neuron poles.

fits_no_version.finding: Under Sort Eval autointerpretability, SAE features from layer 20 of CLIP ViT-L-14 appear the most monosemantic of the 8 layers tested. They also activate most frequently across LAION. The post gives no numbers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a CLIP ViT-L-14 SAE suite, layer-20 residual-stream SAE features are more monosemantic than those of the other tested layers.

record.problems: The authors describe the analysis as preliminary and not demonstrated to high rigor. The monosemanticity result is qualitative, with no scores or uncertainty stated in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction-MSE discussion across image-token positions was left out because it does not bear on the neuron-interpretability claim. The text refers to plots, but their values are not present in the supplied text.

untested.parts: All: no audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles.
All: no native-neuron shares across language models or scales.
All: no analysis of InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons.
All: no share of interpretable native neurons, and no comparison of architectures or tools.
All: no attribution graphs built from neurons.
All: no test of whether explanations predict where a neuron fires.
All: no simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: This is a short LessWrong resource-release post. The plots and per-layer scores are not in the text. The study is irrelevant to the native-neuron claim except as tangential SAE work.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or their job counts.
No comparison of neuron-pole shares across models or scales.
No analysis of InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons or recursive generalization.
No estimate of the share of interpretable native neurons, comparison of architectures or tools, or test of the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
No attribution-graph reconstruction or test of whether native neurons suffice as circuit units.
No test of explanations against held-out activating examples.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.measure: Relative monosemanticity of SAE features by layer, assessed with Sort Eval Autointerpretability
rows.baseline: Other tested layers; no numerical baseline stated
rows.value: Layer 20 seems to be the most monosemantic layer.
rows.note: Qualitative ranking only; it is about SAE features, not native neuron poles, and the text reports no numerical score or share.
rows.check: The subject is SAE features, not native neurons, and the value is a qualitative ranking with no score or baseline number. The state 'observed' has no version to be observed against. It is better treated as cannot_determine, or recorded under fits_no_version only.
